sources.note: Studies how far a fixed model improves when given more inference compute, and shows that allocating that compute adaptively per prompt by difficulty beats a uniform best-of-N budget by more than 4x.
sources.title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters

sources.note: Diagnoses label-free RLVR's collapse as a shortcut in which the same answer-level consensus signal both estimates the reward and receives the gradient, and fixes it by masking the answer span from updates entirely — so a reward can only be raised by improving the reasoning that produces the answer.
sources.title: Don't Peek at the Answer: Outcome-Masked Group Relative Policy Optimization for Label-Free RLVR

sources.note: Formalizes test-time scaling as budgeted inference over a model's implicit prefix tree, separates three structurally different regimes that a single scalar budget conflates, specifies what a reproducible inference protocol must declare, and releases 1.9 million traces — with the empirical section showing a selection score that makes accuracy fall from 75.56% to 65.83% as the candidate bank grows.
sources.title: Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning LLMs: Inference Regimes, Evaluation, and Reproducibility

sources.note: Couples KV-cache compression and generation-length control under a single process-reward signal, compressing harder at high-reward reasoning steps and stopping early when confidence is high.
sources.title: Fewer Tokens, Smaller Cache: Reward-Coordinated Efficient Reasoning

sources.note: Reformulates test-time reasoning as compute allocation over partial trajectories under a hardware budget, and runs a zero-sum beam search over reasoning steps that prunes weak traces and immediately re-spends the freed capacity by branching from high-scoring prefixes.
sources.title: Thought-Level Beam Search for Reasoning

sources.note: Replaces uniform test-time compute allocation with a training-free agent that picks reasoning tools, a search strategy and an exploration parameter per problem, using a process reward model both to prune within a trajectory and to select across iterations.
sources.title: What If We Allocate Test-Time Compute Adaptively?

sources.note: Proves that parameterizing an outcome reward as the log-likelihood ratio between a policy and a reference model makes the per-step Q value fall out of the same model for free, so a process reward model can be obtained by training an outcome reward model on response-level labels alone.
sources.title: Free Process Rewards without Process Labels

sources.note: Formalizes 'spend test-time compute well' as a meta-reinforcement-learning problem — treating one long output stream as a sequence of episodes and scoring it by cumulative regret over tokens — and trains against a dense progress bonus that outcome-only reward cannot express.
sources.title: Optimizing Test-Time Compute via Meta Reinforcement Fine-Tuning

sources.note: A position paper arguing that reading a reasoning model's intermediate tokens as 'reasoning' or 'thinking' is unsupported by the available evidence and actively harmful, and collating experiments in which trace semantics and solution accuracy come apart.
sources.title: Position: Stop Anthropomorphizing Intermediate Tokens as Reasoning/Thinking Traces!
